evidence.detail: Model construction receives this object as its reusable allocation context, sets the current vertex/face counts, and obtains model vertex, face, color, priority, alpha, group and particle arrays from it.
The class owns a slot-keyed HashMap of reusable int[], boolean[] and byte[] arrays plus reusable VertexNormalBuffer and FaceNormalBuffer objects; count changes invalidate or resize workspace state.

Its nested enums preserve TRIANGLE/VERTEX element categories, INT_ARRAY/FLAG_ARRAY/BYTE_ARRAY storage kinds, and model-specific slots including FACE_X, VERT_X, PRIORITIES, ALPHAS, COLOR and PARTICLES.

candidates.note: ModelWorkspace names the reusable model-decoding/render-preparation allocation context; it is a semantic role name rather than an original-identifier claim.

evidence.detail: The enum has exactly two surviving constants: TRIANGLE and VERTEX.
ModelWorkspace maps TRIANGLE to its current face/triangle count and VERTEX to its current vertex count when allocating slot arrays.

candidates.note: ModelElementType directly reflects the surviving TRIANGLE/VERTEX enum vocabulary.

evidence.detail: Surviving enum constants are model-array roles: FACE_X, FACE_Y, FACE_Z, COL_X, COL_Y, COL_Z, INFO, PRIORITIES, ALPHAS, COLOR, VERT_TRANS_GROUPS, VERT_GROUPS, VERT_X, VERT_Y, VERT_Z, PARTICLES and PARTICLE_PRIORITIES.
Each enum value carries one ModelElementType and one ModelArrayType, and ModelWorkspace uses the enum value itself as the HashMap key for allocating/reusing the corresponding array.

candidates.note: ModelArraySlot is the conservative name for the typed key identifying one reusable model array role.

evidence.detail: The enum has exactly three surviving constants: INT_ARRAY, FLAG_ARRAY and BYTE_ARRAY.
ModelWorkspace dispatches on this enum to allocate int[], boolean[] or byte[] storage for a ModelArraySlot.

candidates.note: ModelArrayType directly reflects the surviving array-storage enum vocabulary.
